sections.name: body
sections.value:
# Pane seeks still carry sorting and index maintenance

For pane-filtered registry lists, account for both the indexed candidate
walk and result ordering. The B1 query at PR 312 searches seats_by_pane,
then sorts its matching rows with a temporary B-tree for ORDER BY id.
That removes the full-history walk, not the matching-row decoding or
sort. Inserts and upserts that assign pane pay index maintenance even
when assigning the same value; state-only updates leave that index alone.

Keep SQL benchmark protocols attached to their numbers. The independent
3,252-row copy measured 0.730 -> 0.224 ms CPU for 112 matching rows,
including Python tuple materialization; the author's sqlite3 CLI
0.62 -> 0.07 ms is not the same protocol. Batched write overhead was
0.435-0.551 microseconds per relevant statement, excluding commit/fsync.

The performance verdict at 6f4c3b9010109bf5532864e48dcaa59d97603050
contains the complete SQL, migration and live BEFORE receipts.
POST /v1/whoami measured 2.10584 ms active wall/completion at 11.1605/s,
with host load 97.551 -> 111.161; do not call this quiet or exclusive CPU.
Deployed AFTER remains owed; performance/312 stays held until merge.

Optional C34 follow-up: a plan test against an exported SQL constant
does not catch deletion of the runtime branch selecting it.

**magicWand:** a read-only cost-window command collecting route active/held,
PID/start/build, CPU/RSS, load and cohorts together.

**difficulties:** C25 leaves local TS/full-gate proof CI-only; preserve
exact-head successful-job artifact IDs, and distinguish benchmark engines
and materialization from deployed latency.
